evals.prompt: Use my design philosophy to design the UI for a small macOS menu-bar app that shows our team's on-call schedule and lets me hand over a shift. There's no existing code yet; it's for about 40 SREs.
evals.expected_output: Works through understanding (users, moment, priorities, platform limits of macOS menu-bar apps) before choosing a direction; derives an identity that fits a native macOS utility (not the Recall palette or bottom composer); names one novelty moment (likely the handover); produces a SYSTEM.md, tokens and a guard test alongside the implementation; verifies states including no schedule and offline.
evals.name: oncall-menubar
assertions: States users, their moment and ordered priorities before choosing a direction
Names one deliberate novelty moment tied to the product's differentiator
Identity derived from this product's context (no reuse of the Recall extension palette)
All colours come from tokens; no literal colours in component styles
Dark mode is designed
Verified in a rendered build (screenshots saved)
Writes down a project design system with reasons for its values
Designs the non-happy states (empty, loading, error/offline as relevant)
Faithful to macOS menu-bar conventions and a realistic popover size

evals.prompt: Redesign our internal incident metrics dashboard (in ./dashboard) using my design philosophy. It's shown on a TV in the ops room and on laptops. Brand guide is in ./brand/guide.md.
evals.expected_output: Reads the existing code and the brand guide first and takes the palette from the brand; designs for two contexts (wall display at distance, laptop) with density decided per context; uses a dataviz skill for chart encoding if available rather than duplicating it; audits the current dashboard with measured weaknesses; verifies at TV and laptop sizes in both themes.

evals.prompt: can you apply my design philosophy to the onboarding flow of our mobile banking app? users are older customers switching from branches. keep it accessible
